newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light in talks on deferring plant.
newsitem.headline: China Light in talks on deferring plant.

text.p: China Light and Power Co Ltd has entered into talks with the Hong Kong government on the deferral of two units of its Black Point power plant, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

"China Light and Power (CLP) and CAPCO (Castle Peak Power Company Ltd) confirmed that the companies, while maintaining that any deferral will increase cost over the entire plant life, have entered into discussion with government on the deferral of units seven and eight," the statement said.
CAPCO is a joint venture 40 percent owned by China Light and 60 percent by Exxon Energy Limited.
CAPCO owns all the generating facilities through which China Light purchases power in Hong Kong.
The statement was issued following a debate in the Legislative Council on Wednesday replacing the current scheme of control between the government and the utility.
Legislators recognised in their debate that changes can only be made after mutual agreement between the government, CAPCO and CLP, it said.
China Light and Power said earlier the deferral of units seven and eight could cost the company between HK$200 million and HK$1.5 billion in additional costs.
